title: The drive's fixture suites never run stale bytecode
description: Proven in a scratch copy: with round 1's mtime set back to round 0's (os.utime) wl3/wl4 fail every time with CI's exact signature; with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, or with the generated suite setting sys.dont_write_bytecode before its import, they pass. The gate verdict reuse is content-keyed and not involved; P139 did not touch the path.
desiredOutcome: tests/test_drive_phase.py's generated fixture suites run exactly what their source says whatever the timing of two rewrites, and a case forces the same-second, same-size rewrite so the fix is proven, not hoped

findings.issue: wl3p asserts only the probe's preconditions (same size, v = 2 bytes, mtime put back). It does not assert that a stale bytecode file was ever there to be trusted. wl3/wl4 only go red when the round-0 gate's interpreter actually writes bytecode. Nothing in tools/sweep-selftests.py or tests/_harness.py scrubs PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE (grep found no hit), so a developer or runner that exports it makes the hazard absent. Then wl3/wl4 would pass with the generator switch deleted, and wl3p would not notice.
findings.resolution: Add to wl3p (or a sibling case) a direct assertion that no mine bytecode exists after round 0, under src/__pycache__ and under PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX if set. That goes red on a regression of the generator switch whatever the timing or ambient env, and the mtime probe stays as the end-to-end check.

summary: P141: tests/test_drive_phase.py's generated fixture suite (one generator now) turns bytecode writing off, so a same-size rewrite inside one second runs the new code; wl3 forces that rewrite with os.utime and wl3p asserts the probe applied. One low carried to BUG-29-dau.

tasks.title: The fixture suite generators turn bytecode writing off, and wl3 forces the same-second rewrite
tasks.description: In tests/test_drive_phase.py, make the generated fixture test (the _wf_suite and _house_suite generators, ~1163 and ~9766) set sys.dont_write_bytecode = True before it imports the module under test - one generator if the two can be one without changing what any case asserts. In wl3, between the round-1 writer session and the next signal, restore src/mine.py's mtime to its pre-round-1 value with os.utime, and assert the two versions are the same size and the mtime took, so the probe cannot silently stop applying. Red first: with the generator unchanged the frozen-mtime wl3/wl4 fail; with it they pass.

add: tests/test_drive_phase.py: wl3 forces a same-second, same-size rewrite of the imported module and the resumed round's gate runs the new code

outcome.technical: tests/test_drive_phase.py: (1) wl3 now splits the resume round so that src/mine.py's mtime is restored with os.utime(ns=) to its pre-session value between the resume writer session and the next signal; new case wl3p asserts the two versions are the same size, the new bytes landed (v = 2), and the mtime took (equal st_mtime_ns). (2) _wf_suite emits sys.dont_write_bytecode = True before import mine. (3) the near-duplicate _house_suite and its _TALLY were removed: their generated text was identical line for line apart from the tally constant, which had the same value, so _house_suite is now an alias of _wf_suite and no case's assertion changes. Gates: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py` exit 0 (1/1 files ok, 568 cases); `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --spaced tests/test_drive_phase.py` exit 0 (1/1 files ok, 568 cases). Dependants: sweep-costs.json, drive-phase.py, test__runner_output.py, test_run_test_gate.py, sweep-selftests.py, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and the two docs/research files only reference the suite or names _counting/_follower_cases/_head/_load, none of which I touched, so still correct; _house_suite and _TALLY are the only removed/changed names and a grep of tests/test_drive_phase.py showed no use of _TALLY outside the removed generator. I did not grep other files for _TALLY or _house_suite (the brief lists none as used elsewhere).
outcome.descriptive: The drive's generated fixture suites no longer run stale bytecode, and wl3 forces the same-second same-size rewrite so the fix is proven.

verifiedBy: wl3p: forces the same-size, restored-mtime rewrite of src/mine.py in the resume round and asserts the sizes match, the new bytes landed and the mtime took; the existing wl3/wl4 then prove the resumed gate runs the new code

redFirst.basis: Regression task, expectRedFirst false, and the fix lives in the test file's own generator, so a HEAD throwaway with the test files copied over cannot show a red. The red was watched in the working tree before the generator fix: `python3 tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest --stage wl-block` exited 1 with 'FAIL wl3 nothing is filed while the gate is red; ...', 'FAIL wl4 ...and the close commits: in_progress' and 'SELFTEST FAILED: 12/14 cases passed' while the new probe case wl3p passed (sizes 6/6, mtime_ns equal). After the generator fix the same command exited 0: 'ALL PASS: 14/14 cases passed'.

request: The 3.6.0 release commit's CI went red on tests/test_drive_phase.py wl3/wl4 (linux stress leg, run 40076895652; also P139's run 39927547285): diagnosed as a fixture flake - two same-size rewrites of src/mine.py inside one whole second leave a .pyc Python still trusts, so the gate runs the old code
